title: A counterexample to the Albertson-Berman conjecture about induced forests in planar graphs
summary: For a graph $G$, denote by $a(G)$ the number of vertices in the largest induced forest in $G$. The Albertson-Berman conjecture, which had been open since 1979, states that $a(G) \geq \frac{n}{2}$ for every simple planar graph $G$ on $n$ vertices. Although the Albertson-Berman conjecture was recently resolved in the negative by constructing a counterexample with the help of AI, we independently found a counterexample to the Albertson-Berman conjecture without AI and present it in this article.
